mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in housing starts signals a robust demand for housing, which in turn drives economic growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 4.5% triggers an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and ultimately producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment signals a strong labor market, which in turn drives consumer spending and economic growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high payroll employment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production signals an increase in economic output, which in turn drives economic growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between housing starts and payroll employment signals a strong demand for housing and a strong labor market, which in turn drives economic growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high housing starts and payroll employment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 4.5% and an increase in the consumer price index above 2% trigger an expansionary monetary policy and high inflation, leading to decreased purchasing power and ultimately producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing cycle with high inflation
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in easing periods with high inflation are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% signals a weak labor market, which in turn drives decreased consumer spending and economic growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between housing starts and retail sales signals a strong demand for housing and consumer goods, which in turn drives economic growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during periods of monetary easing.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high housing starts and retail sales in easing cycles (t-test p > 0.05).
